data.title: Fed's Jefferson says he is taking his policy cues from inflation
data.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said on Friday that, with the economy growing and the labor market stabilized, he is taking his policy cues from inflation, a remark that suggests he may support further interest-rate hikes to bring it under control.

Jefferson joined the 10-2 majority of Fed policymakers who voted at their October meeting to wait for more data to accumulate before considering a rate hike.

"Data received since that meeting have been consistent with economic activity and labor market conditions remaining broadly solid, while inflation readings show persistent price pressures," Jefferson said in remarks prepared for delivery at the University of California, San Diego.

"Accordingly, I see the trajectory of inflation as providing the more important signal for determining the appropriate stance of monetary policy." 

Other Fed policymakers in recent weeks have been explicit that elevated and persistent inflation means they would likely support rate hikes that are bigger or come in quicker succession than the single quarter-point increase the Fed delivered in September. 

Jefferson gave no such guidance.

"Going forward, I believe that further policy adjustments should be determined by carefully examining trends in the data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks," he said. 

Jefferson was more forthcoming about his views on artificial intelligence, which he forecast would boost productivity substantially but gradually, bolstering economic output and income while potentially causing pain for some workers and businesses.

"One risk to my baseline outlook is that the new technology could displace workers much faster than they can adapt and retrain, which could result in an increase in unemployment," he said. "Monetary policy can affect cyclical conditions, like a temporary downturn in employment and spending, but it cannot address the structural factors that determine long-run rates of employment."

AI adoption could also result in higher overall borrowing costs in the economy, if companies find themselves needing to continually increase their investments to keep up with a permanently higher pace of productivity growth, he said.

(Reporting by Ann Saphir; Editing by Edmund Klamann)

data.title: Canada, US make progress on trade deal, Carney says
data.description:
MANILA, Nov 14 (Reuters) - Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Saturday he had held lengthy, substantive talks with US President Donald Trump and the two countries were making progress towards a trade deal, though they had yet to reach an agreement.

Carney, who is in the Philippines for a state visit and meeting with Southeast Asian leaders, also said his country would not walk away from NATO and that the security architecture for a free Europe would be determined by a free Europe and NATO, not Russia.

(Reporting by Mikhail Flores; Editing by William Mallard)

data.title: Binance targets full reopening of withdrawals by next week
data.description:
Nov 14 (Reuters) - Binance said on Saturday that it aims to reopen withdrawals for all remaining networks and assets by the end of next week, as operations normalise for the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange after a security breach linked to North Korea saw $6.3 billion stolen from the platform last month.

"This week, we reopened withdrawals for 87 networks. We will aim to reopen withdrawals for all remaining networks and assets by the end of next week," the company said in an X post.

Binance resumed withdrawals in phases earlier this month, after covering 95% of the $6.3 billion in tokens stolen from its platform in what experts describe as the largest cryptocurrency theft ever.

The FBI and Binance have said North Korea was responsible for the Binance hack, but Pyongyang has denied that. Blockchain investigation firms have attributed it to a North Korean group known as "TraderTraitor".

In its initial report on how hackers pulled off the heist, Binance detailed a multi-stage hacking endeavour that began in June and set off a series of security breaches culminating in the theft on October 29.

The theft has underlined the vulnerability of digital assets to attacks and raised questions about the impact of the hack on Binance, which has vowed to repay customers in full.

The company's finance chief Kaiser Ng left the company just over a week after the heist, to pursue a new venture after more than five years at Binance. He was replaced by longtime finance executive Justin Yek, who was most recently vice-president of finance at Airwallex.

(Reporting by Rhea Rose Abraham and Sathvi G Bhat in Bengaluru; Editing by Alexandra Hudson)

data.title: AI Tops Fed's List of Financial Stability Risks as Concern Surges
data.description:
06:52 PM EST, 11/13/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Artificial intelligence was the most frequently cited risk to US financial stability among market participants surveyed by the Federal Reserve, according to the central bank's semiannual Financial Stability Report released Friday.

About 87% of contacts surveyed in September and October named AI as a salient risk, up from 50% in the spring survey. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York polled 23 professionals at broker-dealers, banks, investment funds and advisory firms.

Respondents cited elevated equity valuations, AI-enabled cyberattacks and complex financing tied to data center investment, the Fed said. A correction in risk assets was the second most-cited risk at 52%, followed by higher long-term interest rates at 48%. Cyberattacks and fiscal debt sustainability were each cited by 43%.

Cyberattacks and fiscal debt sustainability were seen as having the most severe potential consequences, the report said. Mentions of AI, higher long-term rates and cyberattacks rose the most from the spring survey, while fewer respondents cited private credit risks, according to the report.

The Fed said advanced computing-related debt issuance topped $680 billion as of October, roughly five times the 2023 total. It said the largest US bank holding companies have close to $1 trillion of exposure to large technology firms, data center developers, related special purpose vehicles, private credit vehicles and utilities.

The Fed said the survey reflects respondents' views and not those of the Fed Board or the New York Fed.

data.title: Modi summons telecom secretary over website takedowns, sources say
data.description:
NEW DELHI, Nov 14 (Reuters) - Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's office summoned the telecommunications secretary on Saturday to explain how officials ordered the takedown of more than 100 websites based on court orders that Reuters revealed were fake, two government sources said.

The intervention from Modi's office signals intensifying scrutiny after Reuters revealed on Wednesday that telecom officials directed internet providers to block 129 illegal betting websites based on fake High Court orders which were emailed to officials by people posing as lawyers.

While online betting is illegal in India, the case has raised concerns that a lack of safeguards in India's content-takedown system could allow falsified court documents to be used to block legitimate websites.

The findings have triggered one criminal investigation by state police against unknown persons for forgery and cheating. 

Modi's office summoned Telecom Secretary Amit Agrawal to appear and explain the lapse, cutting short Agrawal's trip to another state, said the two government officials with knowledge of the matter.

Agrawal is the most senior bureaucrat in the telecommunications ministry, which oversees everyone from big telecom operators to internet providers.

"The action taken by the Department of Telecommunications against betting accounts was carried out through the relevant field officers," said one of the people.

Agrawal and his ministry did not respond to Reuters queries, and neither did Modi's office.

Court precedents generated using AI have caused concerns among judges the world over. India's Supreme Court in July set aside a tribunal's orders that relied on non-existent judgments, and a US judge recently disqualified lawyers over use of fabricated legal citations.

On Friday, Reuters reported that the telecoms ministry had initiated an internal investigation into the alleged fraud, while police have sought ministry records as part of a criminal investigation.

The two state court orders Reuters revealed were fake, based on comments from police and the court registry, contained fabricated court logos and seals, ​as well as a fake QR code. 

They were for months available publicly on the Department of Telecommunications' website, along with correspondence that showed government officials ordering internet providers to remove the websites.

On Saturday, one of the fake court orders was still accessible on the government's website, while one had been removed.

(Reporting by Aftab Ahmed, Munsif Vengattil and Aditya Kalra; Editing by Stephen Coates)

data.title: Tesla invites select customers to buy Cybercab for personal use
data.description:
TOKYO, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Tesla said on Friday it was inviting select customers to buy the Cybercab for personal use, marking a push towards delivering fully designed autonomous vehicles to customers.

-- Tesla posted the announcement on X with an image of the golden butterfly door two-seater, priced at $29,990 with an "Autonomy Subscription" of $299 a month.

-- Chief Executive Elon Musk said in a post on X that the offering would be available nationwide as Tesla receives regulatory approval

-- "The monthly fee is too high," Musk said, adding that it should match the cost of Tesla Full Self Driving and connectivity for other models, which is about $115 per month

-- The EV maker aims to start selling its Cybercab robotaxis to the public by the end of this year, Lars Moravy, Tesla's vice president of vehicle engineering, said last month

-- The Cybercab will work unsupervised in all the same geo locations as the robotaxi, Tesla's head of artificial intelligence, Ashok Elluswamy, said in a separate X post

-- Tesla launched its unsupervised robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, in June 2025, expanded the offering to Dallas and Houston in April 2026 and rolled it out in Miami in July 2026

(Reporting by Sathvi G Bhat in Bengaluru; Editing by William Mallard and Emelia Sithole-Matarise)

data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Stocks mostly ease with tech, Nvidia concerns; airline shares fall late in session
data.description:
(Updates with closing US market levels)

* Nasdaq, S&P 500 end lower

* Oil prices decline for the week

* Dollar extends gains

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Elizabeth Howcroft

NEW YORK/PARIS, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Stock indexes mostly fell on Friday as technology shares sold off amid concerns about US chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ), while the dollar was at a 19-month high.

Airline shares dropped in the final minutes of the regular US session after the US Federal Aviation Administration issued a national ground stop of all departing flights. The agency said this was "due to extraordinary circumstance and reasons for safety" after it earlier reported serious air traffic control communications issues. The NYSE Arca airline index closed down 1.4%.

The Nasdaq and S&P 500 ended lower, but all three of the major US stock indexes and the pan-European STOXX 600 registered gains for the week.

Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday as Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO could have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy and the broader AI industry and supply chain given his push to preserve access to the Chinese market and close ties with US President Donald Trump. Huang stepped down after revelations of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for China.

The Financial Times reported that Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Huang.

The Philadelphia semiconductor index was down 3.4% and shares of Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) were sharply lower. Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares finished 2% lower.

"Traders probably weren't excited about carrying positions into the weekend," said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services in Hammond, Indiana.

"A lot of attention is still going to be paid next week to Nvidia ( NVDA )," he said. The company is due to report quarterly results on Tuesday after the closing bell.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 50.46 points, or 0.10%, to 52,347.55, the S&P 500 fell 30.73 points, or 0.40%, to 7,561.67 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 229.82 points, or 0.91%, to 25,136.27. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 both snapped a four-week streak of declines.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 4.15 points, or 0.37%, to 1,112.12.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index ended up just 0.02%, but recorded its best week since late June as strong earnings and a rotation out of tech globally helped investors look past geopolitical risks and the volatility involving AI stocks.

A global outage of Microsoft Outlook and Teams was easing on Friday after more than 24 hours of disruption crippled online communications across businesses and governments, though the company said it still had no timeline for full recovery of services.

US 2-YEAR YIELDS HAVE LARGEST WEEKLY RISE IN OVER TWO YEARS

The US dollar index gained for a fourth straight day. Traders this week have been ramping up bets on faster interest rate increases following the consumer price data and hawkish Federal Reserve official commentary.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.17% to 103.40. It hit its highest since April 2025. The euro was down 0.29% at $1.1021.

Investors digested a report showing the US October Producer Price Index for final demand was slightly softer than expected, but still shot up 6.5% year over year. It followed a hotter-than-expected US consumer prices reading earlier this week.

Traders see rising odds that the US central bank could hike rates by a larger-than-usual 50 basis points in December, or raise rates by 25 basis points at each of the next three meetings.

"Inflation is stubbornly high and the Fed's going to need to act a little bit quicker and a little bit more aggressively," said Molly Brooks, US rates strategist at TD Securities.

Fed funds futures traders are pricing in an 11% chance of a 50-basis-point hike at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting, which was seen as having zero probability a week ago, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool.

Treasury yields briefly dipped after the PPI data, but interest-rate-sensitive 2-year Treasury yields had the largest weekly increase in over two years.

The 2-year note yield was last up 0.34 basis point at 4.867%. It earlier reached 4.892%, the highest since October 14. It registered the biggest weekly increase since the first week of October 2024.

Oil prices were little changed on Friday, but declined for a second straight week. Washington's focus on blockading Iran and ramping up other economic pressures allayed fears of renewed direct conflict in the Iran war.

Brent futures settled at $95.84 a barrel, up 2 cents, or 0.02%. US West Texas Intermediate futures finished at $88.56 a barrel, down 18 cents, or 0.20%. Both Brent and US crude declined for the week.

(Reporting by Caroline Valetkevitch in New York and Elizabeth Howcroft in Paris; additional reporting by Karen Brettell and Rae Wee; Editing by Kate Mayberry, Stephen Coates, Sharon Singleton, Tomasz Janowski, Alexander Smith and Sanjeev Miglani)

data.title: Microsoft restores service to Outlook and Teams after global outage
data.description:
Nov 14 (Reuters) - Microsoft said on Saturday that services had fully recovered across Teams, Outlook and its other products, ending a global outage that crippled online communications for businesses and governments for over 24 hours.

"We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions," the company posted on X.

Microsoft had said server issues were behind the incident that also affected its Copilot AI assistant, and that it was not aware of any malicious activity, ruling out AI as the cause. 

Outlook and Teams are two of the most widely used workplace applications with hundreds of millions of users. The outage prevented people from performing essential functions such as sending emails, managing calendars and hosting virtual meetings.

It affected government agencies from Australia and Japan to the United States, caused delays at trading firms, hindered some companies from publishing earnings and prompted airlines to warn customers of communication lags, according to public statements.

Organizations that host Microsoft services on their own servers, rather than in the cloud, were somewhat spared. 

ANOTHER OUTAGE FOR MICROSOFT 

The outage, reports of which started climbing around 1725 GMT on Thursday according to Ookla, is one of the longest in Microsoft's history and the second disruption to its services this year.

Microsoft said the outage specifically hit features tied to Exchange Online - its cloud-based email and scheduling hub - leaving unconnected applications operational.

The incident deepens questions about the global reliance on a handful of Big Tech companies that supply both the essential software and the cloud infrastructure that underpins it. 

It also highlighted the dependence on Microsoft's workplace software, with outage reports spiking as employees began their workdays across Asia and Europe, according to Downdetector's parent company, Ookla.

Downdetector logged more than 7.4 million reports worldwide, peaking at nearly 20,000 a minute, more than 1,500 times normal levels.

"It shows how much of the working day now runs through one provider's email and collaboration tools," said Luke Kehoe, lead industry analyst at Ookla.

Microsoft shares closed flat at $523.88 on Friday. The stock has gained roughly 8% so far this year.

Disruptions and financial losses from the outage could result in numerous insurance claims, but the overall hit to insurers is expected to be limited, said Mario De Cicco, vice president of European financial institutions at Morningstar DBRS.

De Cicco estimated global insured losses from the incident at between $300 million and $500 million, well below the $400 million to $1.5 billion financial toll from the 2024 CrowdStrike outage that crashed more than 8 million Windows-based computers and caused widespread disruptions.

Microsoft also faced an outage with its 365 services in January this year and in October last year. Last month, it reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that impacted its suite of productivity software and a range of industries worldwide.

"The bigger worry is that this is not the first Microsoft 365 outage this year," said Josh Gilbert, a market analyst at trading platform eToro. 

"If reliability starts to look like a recurring problem, it hands every IT department a reason to think twice before putting even more of their business in one provider's hands." 

Still, some analysts have questioned whether such incidents can push customers on to rivals due to the steep switching costs of replacing tools embedded so deeply in daily operations. 

TRADES HAD TO BE CONFIRMED BY FAX

A spokesperson for the UK government said it was working with Microsoft to find a solution for the outage that hit organizations such as the NHS and London's Metropolitan Police.

Lack of access to emails and other services was impacting the Metropolitan Police's ability to report some crimes online, though its ability to respond to calls was not affected.

The NHS said its local services were turning to alternate measures such as using IT systems or paper records. 

For businesses, the fallout was widespread. 

European exchange operator Euronext reported email disruptions, British insurer Aviva activated backups for its earnings calls and Danish shipping giant Maersk warned customers of delayed updates.

American AI giants OpenAI and Anthropic also faced issues with Microsoft connectors that were later resolved, while Indian airlines IndiGo, Akasa Air and Air India said their email support services were impacted.

The outage also disrupted fund management at Taiwanese securities firms, life insurers, and investment trust companies. One of the companies went as far as cancelling a bond repurchase transaction, a source familiar with the situation told Reuters.

Another Taiwanese financial company resorted to using fax to confirm trades, a second source said.

In the US, electric truck maker Workhorse Group rescheduled its results on Thursday to November 16, while Switzerland's Richemont briefly delayed its first-half results announcement on Friday.

In Australia, where the spy agency and federal police were among organizations caught in the outage, Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke said Microsoft does not suspect a cyberattack.

"The impact that they are dealing with ... is very much on email systems," the minister added.

data.description:
BEIJING, Nov 14 (Reuters) - China and the United States held their first trade council meeting under a bilateral economic and trade consultation mechanism via video link on Friday, China's commerce ministry said on Saturday.

The two sides held "candid, in-depth and constructive discussions" on implementing outcomes from previous trade consultations, including tariffs, a reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement involving $30 billion on each side, agricultural trade and other issues of note, the ministry said.

Both sides will continue to use the council to address trade concerns, expand cooperation and reduce outstanding issues, it added.

data.title: Pfizer, Innovent GLP-1 drugs added to China national insurance for diabetes
data.description:
SHANGHAI/BEIJING, Nov 14 (Reuters) - GLP-1 drugs from Pfizer ( PFE ) and Innovent Biologics ( IVBXF ) will be added to China's state-run health insurance scheme from January 1 for patients with type 2 diabetes, the National Healthcare Security Administration said on Saturday, in a fresh challenge to Danish rival Novo Nordisk.

China has the highest number of adults with diabetes in the world, ​according to an estimate by the International Diabetes Federation. Pfizer's ( PFE ) ecnoglutide and Innovent's mazdutide belong to the class of GLP-1 ​receptor agonist drugs already included in China's state insurance list from firms such ​as Novo, Eli Lilly ( LLY ) and Guangzhou Innogen Pharmaceutical.

Novo's Ozempic joined China's reimbursement list in ​2022, followed by Lilly's Mounjaro and Innogen's efsubaglutide alfa from this year for patients with ​type 2 diabetes. Inclusion in the national reimbursement list makes drugs more widely available ‌in ⁠the country of 1.4 billion people, though an increase in sales volume often comes with lower prices.

The GLP-1 class of weight drugs mimics a gut ⁠hormone to curb appetite and regulate blood sugar in patients with diabetes.

Sales of Ozempic injector pens in the greater China region of mainland China, Taiwan and Hong Kong - Novo's largest market after the US - slipped 7% to about 5.4 billion Danish crowns ($850 ​million) in 2025.

Other treatments to be added to the list include two Eli Lilly ( LLY ) drugs for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, as well as a CAR-T therapy from JW Therapeutics ( JWCTF ), according to company statements.

The CAR-T therapy, which engineers patients' immune cells to recognise and kill cancer cells, was the first to be included in the reimbursement list.

(Reporting by Andrew Silver and Beijing newsroom; Editing by William Mallard)

California real estate entrepreneur Lindsey Hrovat's woman-owned investment company will target aging properties for renovation, modernization and community revitalization, with new construction planned as a next phase

SAN FRANCISCO, Calif. , Nov. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Atlas Equity Ventures LLC, a California-based, woman-owned real estate investment company founded by Lindsey Hrovat, today announced the launch of its value-add acquisition program focused on undervalued residential and multifamily properties in the San Francisco Bay Area. The program will acquire aging properties affected by deferred maintenance, outdated interiors and aging building systems, and improve them through strategic renovations and operational upgrades.

Image: Lindsey Hrovat

Rather than relying on market appreciation, the program is designed to create value through tangible improvements to existing housing, strengthening long-term property performance while providing safer, more comfortable living environments for residents.

Program Focus

Under the program, Atlas Equity Ventures will prioritize residential and multifamily properties where targeted capital improvements can unlock value overlooked by conventional market participants. Planned improvements include:

• Structural repairs and modernization of building systems

• Energy-efficiency upgrades and life-safety enhancements

• Renovations to individual living spaces

• Improvements to property operations and the overall resident experience

"Aging housing doesn't have to be lost housing," said Lindsey Hrovat, founder of Atlas Equity Ventures. "By addressing deferred maintenance and modernizing older buildings, we can improve the quality of homes available to local communities while building long-term value through disciplined, responsible ownership."

Expansion Into New Construction

Following the launch of the acquisition program, Atlas Equity Ventures plans to expand its investment portfolio over the next several years and pursue new construction projects alongside its residential and multifamily acquisitions. The company will continue to prioritize opportunities where capital improvements and effective management can deliver measurable operational and financial benefits.

Experience Behind the Program

The program draws on Hrovat's background in finance, construction accounting and property investment. She holds a bachelor's degree in finance from Saint Mary's College of California and previously managed accounting systems for general contractors, including construction cost accounting, payroll and profit-and-loss analysis. A licensed real estate agent serving the San Francisco Bay Area, she has spent four years managing a personal portfolio of residential rental properties and fix-and-flip projects, and has met California's experience-based qualification requirements to sit for the state's real estate broker licensing examination.

Hrovat also organizes in-person real estate meetups where agents and investors exchange perspectives on market trends, equity building and investment strategy, and will continue those financial education efforts as the company grows.

About Atlas Equity Ventures

Atlas Equity Ventures is a woman-owned real estate investment company founded by Lindsey Hrovat. The company focuses on identifying undervalued residential and multifamily properties with value-add potential. Its investment approach emphasizes strategic renovations, infrastructure improvements, operational efficiency, and long-term property performance. Through disciplined acquisition and asset improvement strategies, Atlas Equity Ventures seeks to create lasting value while supporting improved residential living environments.

data.title: Nvidia fallout throws spotlight on Southeast Asia's AI boom
data.description:
SINGAPORE, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Southeast Asia's chip and data centre industries expect greater scrutiny after news of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy put the spotlight on Singapore and Malaysia, executives and analysts said.

US lawmakers from both parties are pushing for tougher restrictions on China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips after the Huang scandal increased scrutiny of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) role in US national security.

Washington restricts exports to China of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) most advanced AI chips to protect US dominance of the sector, but lawmakers want to close a loophole that allows Chinese firms to rent computing power from overseas data centres and access the systems equipped with the chips remotely.

Tougher regulations could include new export rules and licensing requirements to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore, the Wall Street Journal reported.

The alleged spy, Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, was an executive at a cloud computing firm in Singapore called Megaspeed that has subsidiaries in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Australia and the US.

Megaspeed has been under investigation by Singapore authorities since February last year for potential false declarations in relation to the purchase of servers and other related offences.

"After this case, every operator in the chain will be expected to know its end user. Southeast Asian operators will still get Nvidia chips, but proof of where every chip sits and who it serves is now part of the product," said Ke Yan, head of research at Singapore-based investment research firm Shenton Research.

'POST-DEEPSEEK MOMENT'

Southeast Asia's data centre industry is thriving. Since 2021, Malaysia has approved 385.7 billion ringgit ($94.67 billion) of data centre-related investments in the country, according to the trade ministry, while Thailand has 42 data centres, representing 3,400 MW of IT load and about 750 billion baht ($22.58 billion) in investment as of February.

Indonesia's data centre market was valued at $2.81 billion in 2025.

Gary Goh, CEO of Malaysia-based data centre consultancy Sprint DC, likened the current situation to a "post-DeepSeek moment". "Once the new rules are out, there will be a lot more restrictions for countries like Malaysia. There could be a short- to medium-term market shock to the Malaysian data centre market," said Goh.

The AI boom has boosted the region, with Singapore in August raising its economic growth forecast to 4.5%-5.5% this ​year, from 2.0%-4.0%, citing the AI cycle. In Malaysia, rising data centre development projects pushed the construction sector up 6% in the third quarter of 2026.

Singapore's and Malaysia's trade ministries did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Malaysia on Thursday said it was weighing a law that will allow the government to monitor data centre operations, including their use of high-performance chips, saying it needed to ensure that any chips subject to US restrictions were imported into Malaysia for domestic use, rather than for re-export.

An investor and CEO of an Asian neocloud company, who declined to be named, spent Friday morning in calls with lawyers in the US. "Everyone is still figuring out... Maybe every time you export something, there will be additional process to go through. We are worried about more scrutiny which will make it longer for chips to come through," the CEO said.

In February 2025, Singapore said that while 22% of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) chip sales were booked to entities with operations in Singapore only 1% physically came to Singapore. Singapore has also just charged a fifth person in an AI server fraud case.

Jarick Seet, head of small-mid caps at Maybank, said the region could weather tighter rules. "Singapore itself will be more stringent, I think it's a natural thing that happens. Singapore will tighten rules and the US will tighten rules, but I don't think this will harm Singapore's and Malaysia's prospect of buying chips."

A senior executive at a chip maker in Singapore, who declined to be named, even sees a silver lining. "With Jensen out, then the Chinese will have a harder time getting chips from the US. Maybe it is not a bad thing for the non-US people who will have more access to chips."

If the US slows building data centres following Democratic victories in key data-centre states such as Texas and Georgia in midterm elections, "those companies are going to look elsewhere and likely come to countries that can offer them land and deals and power," the executive said. "Even if we lose a chunk of the China business, I think we will get other companies coming looking for compute." 

(Reporting by Xinghui Kok and Jun Yuan Yong in Singapore, Rozanna Latiff in Kuala Lumpur, Kane Wu and Yantoultra Ngui in Hong Kong; Writing by Kok Xinghui; Editing by Susan Fenton)

data.title: White House denies Hassett departing Trump administration
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The White House denied on Friday that National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett was leaving the Trump administration in the coming weeks.

Earlier on Friday, Semafor, citing three people familiar with the plan, reported that Hassett was departing in the coming weeks and had been inquiring about roles outside the administration since before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, which resulted in Democrats retaking both chambers of the US Congress, delivering a blow for Republican President Donald Trump.

"There is no factual basis for this reporting. Kevin Hassett is a key member of President Trump's economic team and will continue working to advance President Trump's economic policies," a White House official said.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who could hold both roles, and his counselor, David Zervos, are among the people being eyed to replace Hassett, according to Semafor. The report said Hassett's plans could change.

Semafor said Hassett's departure would be the latest in a series of staffing changes at the White House. Last week, Trump replaced his chief of staff, Susie Wiles, with longtime aide Stephen Miller.

The US Treasury Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Hassett served as the chairman of the White House Council of Economic Advisers during Trump's first administration.

He left the role in 2019 but later returned to the White House to serve as a senior adviser to Trump during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Hassett was considered to replace Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell last year, but Kevin Warsh eventually got the role.

(Reporting by Jasper Ward in Washington; Editing by Caitlin Webber)

( DVLT ) (“Datavault” or the “Company”) (OTC: DVLT), today announced that the Company expects its common stock will be eligible to trade on the over-the-counter market (“OTC Markets”) effective with the open of the market on November 17, 2026. The move to OTC Markets follows Nasdaq’s decision to suspend trading in the Company’s common stock effective November 17, 2026, due to the Company’s non-compliance with Nasdaq’s $1.00 minimum bid price requirement set forth in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) and the “low stock price” rule set forth in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A)(iii), which requires a suspension of Nasdaq trading for an issuer that evidences a closing bid price of less than $0.10 per share for ten consecutive business days.

The Company intends to request a hearing before the Nasdaq Hearings Panel to maintain its Nasdaq listing. At the hearing, the Company will present its plan to evidence compliance with the bid price requirement and to request an extension of time to do so and the reinitiation of trading and continued listing of the Company’s securities on Nasdaq as a result thereof.

data.title: FOREX-Dollar set for best week in two months, yen weakens toward 160
data.description:
* Dollar holds firm as traders ramp up rate hike bets

* Fed officials caution on inflation

* Yen just shy of 160 per dollar, stirring intervention worries

* Aussie dollar feels the heat from rising US yields

(Updates headline and prices throughout)

By Chibuike Oguh and Javi West Larrañaga

NEW YORK/GDANSK, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The dollar was on track for its strongest weekly rise in two months on Friday, holding near a 19-month high as rising bets on a larger Federal Reserve rate hike lifted US Treasury yields, while the yen hovered around 160 per dollar and kept traders alert for possible intervention from Tokyo.

Hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials and this week's stronger-than-expected US inflation data have left traders weighing the prospect of a larger-than-usual Fed rate hike next month.

Two-year Treasury yields have risen around 34 basis points so far this week to around 4.87%, on course for their biggest weekly jump since April 2025.

The euro was down 0.26% at $1.103, after hitting its lowest level against the dollar since April 2025. It was on course for its fourth straight week of losses.

The dollar was up 0.47% at 0.839 against the Swiss franc and was set to snap two straight weeks of losses.

"The dollar is still firm and that's driven by a robust jobs report and an acceleration of the CPI," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex. "We've had a series of hawkish comments from Fed officials this week including from (New York Fed President John) Williams and (Fed Governor Christopher) Waller."

Traders are pricing in a roughly 90% chance of a 25-basis-point hike next month, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, was up 0.15% at 103.37, clinging to its highest since April 2025 and on track for its biggest weekly gain since September. That would be its third straight week of gains.

YEN FOCUS

The yen was steady at 159.70 per dollar, around its weakest since early September, fuelling concerns about possible intervention. The currency has weakened about 1% this week, on track for its biggest weekly loss since September.

Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday the government would respond appropriately to currency volatility.

The Australian dollar was down 0.52% at $0.6773. The Aussie is the worst-performing G10 currency against the dollar so far this month. Australia is the only G10 country for which markets are pricing a rate cut next year.

The New Zealand kiwi weakened 0.41% versus the greenback to $0.5525 and was on course for its third straight week of losses.

In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 4.22% to $68,467.26. Ethereum declined 4.02% to $1,934.86.

(Reporting by Chibuike Oguh in New York and Javi West Larrañaga in Gdansk; Editing by Susan Fenton and Edmund Klamann)

data.title: Trump official seeks $50 billion for air traffic control after outage
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The Trump administration boosted its request for air traffic control funding to $50 billion late Friday after a communications issue forced a nationwide groundstop that halted thousands of flights for hours.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and the White House earlier on Friday asked for $30.1 billion to upgrade the United States' aging airports and air traffic control system.

"This is an emergency," Duffy said. "What's more important than having an air traffic control system that actually works?"

The issue impacted the FAA's en route centers that handle traffic between airports. But the Republican-led Senate Commerce Committee said the incident highlights the need to prioritize modernizing those centers over other projects and noted Congress approved $1.9 billion to replace outdated en route centers.

The world's most complex airspace has experienced a series of events in recent years that have disrupted flights and risked safety. In January 2025, a midair collision at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport killed 67 people.

Congress already approved $12.5 billion over five years in July 2025 to upgrade air traffic control and increase the hiring of controllers following complaints about airport ​congestion, flight delays and technology ​problems.

The request from White House Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy seeks $10.1 billion for air traffic control modernization, including $7.2 billion for a common automation platform and controller workstations and $2 billion for cloud computing.

"This investment is critical to complete the modernization of our national airspace - delivering a resilient telecommunications backbone for air traffic controllers, modern hardware and software, state-of-the-art control towers, and world-class airport infrastructure," Duffy and Vought wrote to lawmakers asking for swift action.

Major airlines including American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, United Airlines and Southwest Airlines have expressed support for the request.

The $30.1 billion request also includes $2 billion to replace and improve Federal Aviation Administration air traffic control towers and $18 billion for airport-related projects including $10 billion to modernize or replace aging terminals.

The FAA relies on decades-old ​computers as well as replacement parts bought through auction websites. Last week, it said it would replace by the end of 2028 floppy disks used for weather and other critical information at more than 400 air traffic control facilities.

Vought and Duffy in their letter said the FAA has replaced 68% of legacy copper telecommunications network with high-speed fiber infrastructure.

The administration has called for the Republican-led Congress to approve funding in the final weeks of the year. Democrats are set to take control of Congress in January.

In September, the dual failures of a circuit at a Philadelphia ​air traffic facility and the ​accidental severing of a ⁠fiber-optic cable in New Jersey by a construction crew led to thousands of flights across the densely populated Northeast being delayed or canceled.

(Reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Christopher Cushing and Shri Navaratnam)

data.title: Factbox-Old air traffic control equipment regularly disrupts US flights
data.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - The grounding of all departing flights across the United States on Friday was only the second such shutdown since the September 11, 2001, attacks. But the reason - communications equipment problems - has become increasingly common. 

Last year, Congress approved $12.5 billion for upgrading the Federal Aviation Administration's antiquated air traffic control systems and hiring more controllers. The Trump administration wants Congress to approve another $30 billion to finish the job. 

Here are some of the biggest disruptions in the past three years:

November 13, 2026: Nationwide ground stop

The FAA grounded all departing flights in the United States after air traffic control centers suffered a communications outage. Airlines canceled more than 1,000 flights and delayed nearly 10,000, according to flight-tracking service FlightAware.

September 21, 2026: East Coast

The FAA halted flights to airports in New York, Philadelphia, Boston ​and Washington for eight hours, after the regional Philadelphia air traffic control facility's primary and backup data links failed. About 9,500 US flights were delayed or canceled as a result. The outage coincided with the arrival of 130 world leaders traveling to New York for the annual high-level meeting of the United Nations General Assembly.

September 19, 2025: Dallas

A data service outage at the FAA's Dallas TRACON - or Terminal Radar Approach Control, which manages aircraft between the airport and high-altitude flight, forced the agency to issue ground stops at two Dallas-area airports. More than 1,800 flights were delayed and hundreds were canceled.

The FAA later said contractor L3Harris failed to make sure that redundancies were in place. In response, L3Harris told NBC 5 in Dallas that the "outages at (Dallas) were preventable and are a direct result of lack of U.S. government investment to replace legacy, end-of-life analog telecom circuits." 

One day earlier, an unrelated automation failure in Denver forced the FAA to slow flights into Denver International Airport, causing delays averaging 30 to 45 minutes.

April-May, 2025: Newark, NJ and Philadelphia

Multiple telecommunications outages over several weeks at the FAA's Philadelphia TRACON repeatedly disrupted traffic at Newark, New Jersey. A 90-second outage early in the morning of May 9 caused 380 flight delays and 141 cancellations, according to FlightAware.

During the outage, an air traffic controller told a freighter pilot that "our (radar) scopes just went black again. If you care about this, contact your airline and try to get some pressure for them to fix this stuff."

January 11, 2023: Nationwide ground stop

The FAA issued the first nationwide ground stop since the September 11 attacks, after contractors accidentally deleted files, which disrupted the Notice to Air Missions (NOTAM) messaging system.

More than 10,000 flights were delayed or disrupted due to the 90-minute ground stop.

(Reporting by Dan Catchpole in Seattle; editing by Peter Henderson and Stephen Coates)

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: US flight shutdown exposes deepening air traffic network crisis
data.description:
CHICAGO, Nov 13 (Reuters) - A communications failure that halted flight departures across the United States on Friday has renewed scrutiny of the country's aging air traffic control network, raising questions about its resilience even as the government spends billions of dollars to modernize it.

The Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop, preventing aircraft from departing US airports, following "a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a post on X.

Duffy later attributed the outage to a problem with the FAA's legacy network, saying switches and routers had become overloaded with data and went down. It was not immediately clear what caused the equipment overload.

The FAA lifted the ground stop after more than four hours, but Duffy warned that it would take time for air traffic operations to return to full capacity.

More than 1.5 million passengers were scheduled to depart US airports on roughly 11,000 flights after 4 p.m. ET (2100 GMT), shortly after the ground stop began, according to aviation analytics firm Cirium.

The shutdown came on the same day the White House and Transportation Department sought another $30.1 billion from Congress to upgrade airports and air traffic control, including $10.1 billion for air traffic control modernization.

Much of the system's underlying weakness has been documented for years.

The Government Accountability Office reported in 2024 that the FAA had classified 51 of its 138 air traffic control systems as unsustainable and another 54 as potentially unsustainable. Together, they accounted for more than three-quarters of the systems reviewed.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told Reuters in September that the agency's more than 300 air traffic facilities operated as technological silos, relying in some cases on decades-old computers and telecommunications systems that cannot communicate seamlessly with one another.

Some obsolete equipment requires replacement parts obtained through online auction websites or made using 3D printing.

BACKUP SYSTEMS UNDER STRAIN

An incident in September demonstrated how one communications failure could be compounded by another.

After error messages appeared on a telecommunications circuit serving a Philadelphia air traffic control facility, the FAA's contractor switched to a backup fiber-optic line. A construction crew then accidentally severed that line in New Jersey, contributing to widespread disruption. About 9,500 US flights were delayed or canceled that day.

"When it fails, we just don't have the redundancy that we would get if we had a modern architecture," Bedford said at the time.

Friday's shutdown was the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023, when a failure of the FAA system that distributes critical safety notices to pilots halted departures for less than two hours and disrupted more than 10,000 flights.

Congress approved $12.5 billion in July 2025 to modernize the country's aging air traffic control infrastructure, including telecommunications and radar systems. The administration said Friday that 68% of the FAA's legacy copper telecommunications network had been replaced with high-speed fiber.

But Bedford warned in September that replacing aging copper wires with fiber-optic cables alone would not prevent future outages without a modern telecommunications network.

The overhaul faces challenges beyond securing money.

In September, the Government Accountability Office warned that the FAA lacked a reliable cost estimate and an integrated master schedule for its air traffic control modernization program.

Instead, as of May, it had 11,389 separate project schedules that were not coordinated, raising the risk of repeated work at the same facilities, delays and cost overruns.

The FAA aims to complete the first phase of modernization by December 2028. But the GAO warned that inadequate planning increased the risk of delays, potentially leaving the agency dependent on outdated systems prone to failure for longer.

(Reporting by Rajesh Kumar Singh; Editing by Stephen Coates)

data.title: Trump not expected to raise Alice Huang case with China's Xi, US officials say
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump is not expected to discuss with Chinese President Xi Jinping the case involving a businesswoman whose ties to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang raised national security concerns, US officials said on Friday.

Trump is set to meet with Xi next week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China, as part of a four-day trip to Asia. The meeting will come just days after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Thursday, capping a spectacular fall from the chip industry's heights.

Though semiconductors have been a major flash point in US-China relations, the US president is not expected to raise the latest issue with Xi for now, the officials said,

"When it comes to some of these national security matters and examinations and investigations that are going on in the US, it's probably not something that we're going to read the Chinese in on at this moment," one senior administration official told reporters.

A second US official added: "I don't expect the president to raise it, the Alice Huang issue."

The officials were responding to a reporter's question about whether Trump would raise the allegations involving Alice Huang with Xi.

On Tuesday, the independent members of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board said they hired Wall Street law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation after the New York Times and Wall Street Journal reported on Jensen Huang's relations with the businesswoman, Alice Huang, as well as US authorities' suspicions that she was spying for China.

Beijing has denied she is a spy. Alice Huang could not be reached. Reuters has not independently verified whether Alice Huang was working on behalf of the Chinese government. The Justice Department has said it has not reached any conclusion about Alice Huang's affiliation with the Chinese government.

Jensen Huang apologized in a statement on Sunday for being unfaithful to his wife and for disappointing the company. His statement did not specifically name Alice Huang, a former top executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed International. The two are not related.

(Reporting by Trevor Hunnicutt and Jasper Ward in Washington; Editing by Edmund Klamann)

data.title: US lifts nationwide flight shutdown caused by communications failure
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The US Federal Aviation Administration lifted a nationwide ground stop on Friday after a communications failure at air traffic control centers caused chaos at airports and triggered the longest nationwide shutdown since the September 11, 2001, attacks.

More than 4,700 flights were canceled and 10,000 delayed on Friday, while another 700 had already been canceled for Saturday, according to FlightRadar24. Aviation analysts said it could take days for airlines to restore their schedules after a nationwide grounding that lasted more than four hours.

The Department of Homeland Security said there were no signs the outage was caused by a cyberattack.

The failure is the latest and most dramatic sign of strain on a US air traffic control system beset by equipment and communications problems, controller shortages and aging infrastructure.

The only other nationwide ground stop since the September 11 attacks came in January 2023, when the FAA halted domestic departures for around 90 minutes.

data.title: Jackson's AMTC to Open State-of-the-Art ManuTech Prototyping Center
data.description:
Lean Rocket Lab, JAMA and the Shop Rat Foundation will cut the ribbon Dec. 14, giving startups, manufacturers, students and apprentices a place to scan, design and build real parts

JACKSON, Mich., Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Startups and small to medium-sized manufacturers in the Jackson region will soon be able to go from idea to physical prototype in a single afternoon. The Advanced Manufacturing Training Center (AMTC) consortium, a partnership between the Lean Rocket Lab, Jackson Area Manufacturers Association (JAMA) and Shop Rat Foundation, will open its new ManuTech Prototyping Center with a ribbon cutting on Dec. 14, 2026.

The ribbon cutting anchors the ManuTech LIVE Innovation Experience 2026, a public event from 3:30-6 p.m. at the AMTC, 3517 Scheele Drive in Jackson. Attendees will see startups putting the new center to work and technology companies demonstrating their products on the AMTC's live factory floor.

The ManuTech Prototyping Center brings a complete digital-to-physical workflow under one roof for both physical products and electronic hardware. Users can capture an existing part, refine it as a digital model, and produce it in more than one material and process.

"The ManuTech Prototyping Center will connect digital design with physical production, allowing users to scan objects, develop digital models and produce parts using different manufacturing processes," said Brandon Marken, CEO of Lean Rocket Lab. "Manufacturers need places where they can explore new ideas, see technology in action and understand what's possible before taking the next step. This space will make those opportunities more accessible and give businesses a place to connect innovation with real-world manufacturing needs."

The Center's equipment includes a handheld 3D scanner to capture existing parts and objects as precise digital models; a large-format resin 3D printer for high-detail, smooth-finish prototypes; fused deposition modeling (FDM) 3D printers for fast, durable functional parts and test fixtures; and a computer-aided design workstation using SOLIDWORKS software, the industry-standard engineering software, to modify or design parts from scratch. Additional capabilities for electronics are also being added to the center's current capabilities in the near future.

Lean Rocket Lab leads the center, which is built primarily for startups and small to medium-sized manufacturers that need to test ideas without investing in equipment of their own. However, users won't be on their own: Lean Rocket Lab Entrepreneur-in-Residence Steve Tebbetts, who previously ran a prototyping lab for a Michigan OEM, will guide them through the product development process.

Because the center sits inside the AMTC, it also strengthens the training programs already housed there. JAMA apprentices and Shop Rat Foundation students will gain hands-on exposure to the same scanning, design and additive manufacturing tools that companies are adopting today.

"Manufacturing is changing, and our workforce needs opportunities to learn, adapt and grow alongside that change," said Olivia Steele, executive director of JAMA. "Events like ManuTech LIVE help people see the career possibilities in front of them and understand the role apprenticeship training can play in building a strong manufacturing workforce."

The Shop Rat Foundation, which reaches more than 4,000 young people each year, sees the center as a new entry point into technical careers.

"Getting our youth excited about how things work can open the door to opportunities they may never have considered," said Kelly Kofflin, executive director of the Shop Rat Foundation. "Bringing students, educators and industry together helps make those connections and shows young people that they can have a future in advanced manufacturing."

The ManuTech LIVE event will also feature select startups demonstrating technology and products designed to address practical business and industry challenges. Detect-It, will showcase artificial intelligence-powered vision technology for inspection and defect detection, with a potential demonstration involving parts produced on a CNC machine. Jendamark will demonstrate its Odin Workstation, an AI-powered manufacturing execution system designed for assembly processes. And Machine AI Solutions is expected to showcase technology related to machine data and monitoring.

Additional participating companies include Veriti, which offers a platform that converts 2D engineering drawings into quotes for machine shops; Tackboard, which provides digital maintenance ticketing software; Strain Guard, which makes a physical product designed for RV owners to help protect cables from damage; and Cerebion, which focuses on cybersecurity for industry.

In addition to the Prototypic Center launch, ManuTech LIVE will also feature real-time demonstrations of manufacturing technology within the broader AMTC facility, including a manual machining lab, a welding lab and multiple computer numerical control (CNC) machines. JAMA will also share information on its apprenticeship programs, and the Shop Rat Foundation will highlight its youth STEM programming.

ManuTech LIVE is designed for manufacturers, technology companies, students, educators, community leaders and anyone interested in the technologies and training shaping the region's manufacturing future.

To learn more about the event or to RSVP, visit www.go.leanrocketlab.org/events/manutech 

Event Details:

  • What: Ribbon cutting for the ManuTech Prototyping Center at ManuTech LIVE Innovation Experience 2026
  • When: Monday, Dec. 14, 2026, 3:30–6 p.m. Ribbon cutting at 4:30 p.m.
  • Where: Advanced Manufacturing Training Center (AMTC), 3517 Scheele Drive, Jackson, Mich.
  • RSVP: www.go.leanrocketlab.org/events/manutech

About the AMTC consortium
The Advanced Manufacturing Training Center (AMTC) in Jackson is operated through a partnership between the Jackson Area Manufacturers Association, the Shop Rat Foundation and Lean Rocket Lab. Together, the partners combine apprenticeship training, youth STEM education and startup and small business support in a single facility dedicated to the region's manufacturing future.

About Lean Rocket Lab
The Lean Rocket Lab is a nonprofit organization focused on helping entrepreneurs, startups, and small businesses at every stage of growth. As a designated Michigan Economic Development Corporation (MEDC) Small Business Support Hub, the Lean Rocket Lab delivers practical tools, targeted resources, and hands-on support to help entrepreneurs and innovators move from idea to execution. For more information, please visit leanrocketlab.org.

About JAMA
Jackson Area Manufacturers Association (JAMA) is in the heart of manufacturing in Jackson County and beyond, with a statewide reach across Michigan. We bring together local manufacturers, educators, and industry experts to spark collaboration, fuel innovation and drive growth. Through our Advanced Manufacturing Training Center and apprenticeship programs, we equip students and professionals with the hands-on skills today's workforce demands. For more information, visit jacksonjama.org. 

About The Shop Rat Foundation
The Shop Rat Foundation is a Jackson-based, nonprofit organization with a mission to "ignite interest in manufacturing and professional trades careers among youth through innovation and outreach." The organization's curriculum focuses on computer science, engineering, precision machining, robotics and welding, as well as construction trades; serving over 4,000 youth annually through in-school partnership programs, extracurricular classes and camps, as well as community events focused on opportunities for youth to gain awareness of, engage with and explore careers within the manufacturing and professional trades sectors. data.title: What we know about Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang
data.description:
* Singapore says Alice Huang left in February and is barred from re-entering

* Justice Department has not reached conclusion on whether Huang spied for China, Blanche says

* Alice Huang was in Chinese finance before emerging at Singapore's Megaspeed

By Wen-Yee Lee, Andrew Silver and Laurie Chen

Nov 14 (Reuters) - Alice Huang had a long career in Chinese finance before later emerging as an executive in the global race for artificial-intelligence chips.

Known also as Huang Le, she was a top executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech company that was an Nvidia ( NVDA ) business partner in the Asia-Pacific region. Her reported affair with Jensen Huang led in part to his resignation as Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO on November 12.

Several news organizations, including the New York Times and the Wall Street Journal, have reported that US and other government authorities had suspicions that Alice Huang was spying for Beijing. In the spring of 2026, Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw the drafting of a classified memo detailing intelligence indicating that China's Ministry of State Security had recruited Huang to target Nvidia's ( NVDA ) CEO, the New York Times said.

Reuters has not been able to verify any of the allegations made in the New York Times, along with other media reports, about Huang's suspected spying for China.

Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy. Reuters attempts to reach Alice Huang have been unsuccessful. Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are not related.

Here are more details about what is known about Alice Huang:

SUSPICIONS OF SPYING, GOVERNMENT STATEMENTS

The New York Times reported on November 10 that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had briefed President Donald Trump aboard Air Force One en ​route to China in May about US intelligence indicating Jensen Huang was involved with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy.

The briefing marked at least the second time in seven months that Trump had been told about the intelligence, the Times ​reported, citing people with knowledge of the matter. Reuters was not able to confirm these warnings to Trump.

President Trump said on November 9 that the FBI was looking into the spying allegations. He said Jensen Huang told him he had no idea of the spying allegations, and also said he did not need to act on intelligence when he was briefed.

US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on November 12 that the Department of Justice had not yet reached a conclusion as to whether Alice Huang was a spy for China. CNN reported that day that US intelligence officials are still working to understand their relationship, citing people who say there is disagreement about the strength of the evidence that she was recruited to spy for Beijing.

Singapore's home affairs ministry said on November 12 that it had seized Alice Huang's passport in 2025 while investigating her for other offenses, including buying servers that were exported via Singapore to Malaysia without entering the Singapore market. The ministry said there was insufficient evidence to establish Alice Huang had committed any offenses.

The country's foreign ministry also said it received "limited" help from the US in its probe that began in 2025 into false declarations in the purchase of servers and other related offenses. Alice Huang left the country in February and was barred from re-entering following Singapore's investigation, the ministry said.

TIES TO JENSEN HUANG

The Financial Times reported on November 6 that Alice Huang had a romantic affair with Jensen Huang. On November 8, Jensen Huang released a statement acknowledging an extramarital affair, without naming Alice Huang in the statement.

Reuters has verified photos of Jensen Huang and Alice Huang together at several different events over the last two-plus years, with the earliest dating to December 2023.

ROLE AT MEGASPEED

Huang became the controlling shareholder of Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed International in March 2023, according to Washington-based research group C4ADS, which reviewed corporate records.

In October 2025, the New York Times reported the company was under US investigation over whether it was helping Chinese customers obtain advanced Nvidia ( NVDA ) chips subject to Washington's export controls. China has denied this allegation, and there has been no public finding that Megaspeed violated ​the rules.

Earlier this week, The Information reported that Jensen Huang's ties to Alice Huang facilitated at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia ( NVDA ) chip sales to China.

Megaspeed said on November 12 that it has cooperated with US inspections.

CORPORATE ROLES

Alice Huang previously worked in banking and investment management, according to Chinese fund-industry records and an indexed profile on private-fund database ​Simuwang, which also listed an earlier career in television journalism. She also held senior positions at Shanghai Hexi Investment Management, a Chinese investment firm.

She held senior roles ​at a Shanghai investment firm before her role at Megaspeed, according to financial records, corporate filings and company materials reviewed by Reuters.

(Additional reporting by Reuters staff; writing by David Gaffen; editing by Edward Tobin)

data.title: Democratic senators order Musk to preserve records over Ukraine Starlink access, WSJ reports
data.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - Democratic senators have told Elon Musk to preserve all records related to SpaceX's restrictions on Ukraine's use of its Starlink and Starshield satellite services, The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing a letter.

Ukrainian forces say Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink, is vital for front-line communications and drone operations in their defense against Russian drone and missile attacks.

But in mid-October, Ukrainian officials complained that the service had been restricted without explanation or warning, limiting the military's ability to conduct complicated strike missions against Russian forces and slowing interceptor drones used to shoot down Russian attack drones.

"The October and November restrictions now raise the disturbing possibility that these vulnerabilities persist even within systems on which the U.S. government relies," Senators Jeanne Shaheen and Chris Coons said in the letter to Musk, the report said.

The lawmakers sought SpaceX's records since September 1, including all communications related to Starlink and Starshield in Ukraine as well as communications between Musk, SpaceX executives and the White House and Pentagon, the report said.

Shaheen and Coons said the restrictions raised "serious questions" about SpaceX's control over communications systems critical to national security and criticized what they described as "opaque decision-making," according to the Journal.

Reuters reported in October that an order to limit Starshield service used by Ukrainian forces came from inside the White House. Secretary of State Marco Rubio later disputed that account, saying decisions on Ukraine's access to the service were up to SpaceX and Musk.

Later that month Ukraine said Starlink and Starshield were operating normally. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Thursday, however, that Ukrainian military units had again recorded disruptions to Starshield communications.

(Reporting by Carlos Méndez in Mexico City, Editing by Franklin Paul and Stephen Coates)

data.title: Exclusive-Ex-Nvidia CEO misled top lawyer on affair with Chinese businesswoman, sources say
data.description:
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled several of the company's leaders, including general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld, about the nature of his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, with whom he had an affair, according to two people familiar with the matter and internal correspondence reviewed by Reuters.

Reuters reviewed several exchanges from October on condition of not quoting verbatim from the messages. The news agency is the first to report on this correspondence.

On Thursday, Huang resigned as Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO, a spectacular fall from the chip industry's heights where he was a pioneer of technology central to the recent boom in artificial intelligence.

He apologized in a statement on Sunday for being unfaithful to his wife and for disappointing the company. His statement did not specifically name Alice Huang, a former top executive of Nvidia ( NVDA ) customer Megaspeed International, whom the US was investigating for potentially spying for China. Jensen Huang and Alice Huang share a last name but are not related.

The New York Times earlier this week reported Huang also had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia ( NVDA ) employee, and Reuters reported on Thursday that Huang had another intimate relationship with a different Nvidia ( NVDA ) employee.

Teter did not respond to a request for comment. Wagonfeld did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A representative for ex-CEO Huang and an Nvidia ( NVDA ) spokesperson declined to comment. A phone call and email to contact information listed on a business card for Alice Huang went unanswered.

During the autumn of 2025 and in October 2026, in response to press queries that drew some Nvidia ( NVDA ) leaders' attention to his relationship with Megaspeed and Alice Huang, Huang at both times described their interactions as appropriate, the people said, speaking on the condition of anonymity. Reuters only reviewed messages from the exchanges in October, not the ones from 2025.

In two separate messages in October, Huang told Nvidia ( NVDA ) leaders, including Teter and Wagonfeld, that the interactions reflected standard business dealings with customers. In other messages, Huang affirmed the routine nature of his interactions with Megaspeed.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Huang also discussed taking legal action against the New York Times after it published an article in October of last year that drew attention to his meetings in public with Alice Huang, the people said.

That article had prompted Jensen Huang to communicate with some Nvidia ( NVDA ) leaders in 2025 about their interactions, which he did not describe as an affair, the people said. Ultimately, neither Nvidia ( NVDA ) nor Huang filed a lawsuit against the paper. A spokesperson for the New York Times said the paper received no legal demand.

It is unclear when his relationship with Alice Huang became intimate. Photos posted online and verified by Reuters show them together in the US, China and elsewhere, dating as far back as December 2023.

On November 10, the independent members of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board said they hired Wall Street law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation after the New York Times and Wall Street Journal reported on Huang's relations with Alice Huang, as well as US authorities' suspicions that she was spying for China. Beijing has denied she is a spy.

Reuters has not independently verified whether Alice Huang was working on behalf of the Chinese government.

Jensen Huang said in an interview with Bloomberg published on October 29 that the US government had not informed him about its suspicions regarding Alice Huang.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stock has fallen more than 30% since its October 6 closing high, erasing more than $1.8 trillion from its market capitalization.

(Reporting by Jeffrey Dastin and Max A. Cherney in San Francisco; additional reporting by Krystal Hu; Editing by Kenneth Li, Lincoln E. Feast and David Gaffen)
